title: Sharpening comparison on saturated fraction charts and ordered towers
statement:
Use fine monoschemes, fans, coherent monoid ideals, saturated blowup towers, recursive pullback, and contraction as in [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] and [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Let $\mathscr C$ be the full category of fine monoschemes with finite affine covers such that both their ordinary stalk group completions and the group completions of their sharpened stalks are torsion free. For $M\in\mathscr C$, put $F=M^\sharp$ and let $\lambda:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M/\mathcal M^\times$ be the quotient. Image and inverse image under $\lambda$ are mutually inverse bijections on coherent ideal subsheaves, allowing the empty ideal. They preserve nonemptiness and the whole ideal and commute with the ideal generated by images under any morphism between objects of $\mathscr C$.

More explicitly, for an affine chart $P$ of $M$, set $U=P^\times$ and $B=P/U$. For any splitting $P\simeq B\oplus U$ over $B$, any nonempty finitely generated ideal $J\subset B$, and $a\in J$, the corresponding ideal of $P$ is $J\oplus U$ and the blowup chart and its saturation are respectively
$$B[J-a]\oplus U,\qquad (B[J-a])^{\mathrm{sat}}\oplus U.$$
Here $B[J-a]\subset B^{\mathrm{gp}}$ is generated by $B$ and the differences $b-a$ for $b\in J$. The sharpening of the saturated chart is canonically the fan chart for $J$; this identification is independent of the splitting and of generator representatives. On the overlap of the $a$- and $b$-charts its maps are induced by the identities of fractions after localization at $b-a$ and $a-b$, with the cocycle identity on triple overlaps. These maps give a canonical isomorphism $(\operatorname{Bl}^{\mathrm{sat}}_I M)^\sharp\simeq\operatorname{Bl}^{\mathrm{sat}}_{\lambda(I)}F$ over $F$, compatible with restrictions. The saturated blowup remains in $\mathscr C$.

For every finite ordered saturated blowup tower on $F$ there is a unique corresponding tower on $M$, up to its canonical identifications over $M$, whose centers have the specified images under $\lambda$ at every stage; sharpening is inverse to this construction. The correspondence retains all original indices and ideal centers and commutes with recursive pullback along smooth monoscheme morphisms. Its chart maps under pullback are the substitutions of the images of the same fractions.

source.place: ILO VIII 3.1.17--3.1.25(i)--(iii), pp.101--102; fraction-chart and finite-tower comparison (returned proof steps 1--3). No Stacks tag states this monoidal-geometric result.

proof.text:
On an affine monoscheme chart write $q:P\to B=P/U$, $U=P^\times$. The integral-sharpening exactness lemma makes $B$ integral and identifies the kernel of $P^{\mathrm{gp}}\to B^{\mathrm{gp}}$ with $U$. Every ideal is stable under adding and subtracting $U$. Consequently primes of $P$ are inverse images of primes of $B$, and $D(p)$ corresponds to $D(q(p))$; this gives the same underlying topological space. On these basic opens the map $P[p^{-1}]\to B[q(p)^{-1}]$ is surjective. An element above a unit of the latter is a unit of the former: if $q(x)+q(y)=0$ after localization, then $x+y\in U$ after localization, so $x$ has inverse $y-(x+y)$. Two elements have the same image precisely when their difference is in $U$. It follows, also after quotienting by all localized units, that
$$P[p^{-1}]/P[p^{-1}]^\times\simeq B[q(p)^{-1}]/B[q(p)^{-1}]^\times.$$
The affine fan localization-section lemma identifies these quotients with the sections and stalks of the sharpened sheaves, with their restriction maps. Thus the sharpening of this chart is canonically the affine fan of $B$.

For an ideal $I\subset P$, $q^{-1}(q(I))=I$: if $q(p)=q(i)$ with $i\in I$, then $p=i+u$ for a unit $u$. For an ideal $J\subset B$, surjectivity gives $q(q^{-1}(J))=J$. If $I$ is generated by $p_1,\ldots,p_r$, its image is generated by $q(p_1),\ldots,q(p_r)$; conversely, lifts of finite generators of $J$ generate its inverse image. Allow $r=0$, giving the empty ideal. These formulas commute with localization, so by Step 1 they identify coherent ideal subsheaves and their inverse images on overlapping affine opens. Equality is checked on stalks, so the local bijections glue. They preserve emptiness and the whole ideal. For a monoid homomorphism $h:P\to Q$, both orders of taking an image ideal and sharpening give the ideal generated by $\overline h(q(I))$ in $Q/Q^\times$, since a homomorphism sends units to units. The same stalkwise equality proves the asserted compatibility for every monoscheme morphism in $\mathscr C$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.18, 3.1.25(i), pp.101--102; explicit ideal and finite-generator argument.

proof.text: The hypotheses needed for a splitting hold on every affine chart $P$. At its closed point, the ordinary stalk is $P$: only units are inverted. The sharp stalk is $B$, by Step 1 with $p=0$. Hence both $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ and $B^{\mathrm{gp}}$ are torsion free by the definition of $\mathscr C$. Apply the fine-monoid unit-splitting lemma to obtain a section $j:B\to P$ and an isomorphism $(b,u)\mapsto j(b)+u$ from $B\oplus U$ to $P$ over $B$. Under any such splitting, the inverse image of $J$ from Step 2 is exactly $J\oplus U$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.11 and 3.1.25(ii), pp.100,102; splitting justified by the existing unit-splitting lemma with both torsion-free hypotheses.

proof.text:
Choose a finite nonempty generating set $E$ for $J$. In the blowup chart at a lift $(a,u_a)$ of $a\in J$, the unsharpened monoid is generated by $B\oplus U$ and
$$(b,u_b)-(a,u_a)=(b-a,u_b-u_a),\qquad b\in J,\ u_b\in U.$$
Since all of $U$ is already present, this is exactly $C_a\oplus U$, where $C_a=B[J-a]$. It suffices to use $b\in E$: if $b=e+c$ with $e\in E$, $c\in B$, then $b-a=(e-a)+c$. Thus $C_a$ is fine, generated by a finite generating set of $B$ and the finitely many $e-a$, and $C_a^{\mathrm{gp}}=B^{\mathrm{gp}}$ because $B\subset C_a\subset B^{\mathrm{gp}}$. These are precisely the ordinary blowup charts prescribed by the monoscheme definition. Lean proof by S6: the finite ideal closure membership theorem writes every b in J as c*d with d in E; hence b/a is of(c)*(of(d)/of(a)). The closure universal property proves equality with the all-J chart. For a given splitting e, the completion lift is bijective: lift the first-factor section and combine it with the unit-factor map for a left inverse; fractions of e inverse images give surjectivity. Every (of(b),u) is already the image of a base generator, so all unit coordinates are present. Each fraction generator then has exactly its sharp fraction as first coordinate, and multiplication by an available unit removes its second coordinate. These two inclusions prove the ordinary product-chart equality without fineness or torsion-freeness assumptions beyond those retained in the signature.

Inside $B^{\mathrm{gp}}\oplus U$, a positive multiple of $(c,u)$ lies in $C_a\oplus U$ if and only if that multiple of $c$ lies in $C_a$. Therefore
$$(C_a\oplus U)^{\mathrm{sat}}=C_a^{\mathrm{sat}}\oplus U.$$
The finite-saturation lemma makes $C_a^{\mathrm{sat}}$ fine and says that saturation commutes with localization. The units of a product $R\oplus U$ with a group are exactly $R^\times\oplus U$: an inverse exists precisely when the first coordinate has an inverse. The projection therefore gives
$$(C_a^{\mathrm{sat}}\oplus U)/(C_a^{\mathrm{sat}}\oplus U)^\times\simeq C_a^{\mathrm{sat}}/(C_a^{\mathrm{sat}})^\times.$$
The same calculation on every basic localization, followed by the localization-section lemma, identifies the sharpening of the saturated monoscheme chart with the fan chart prescribed for $J$. Lean proof by S6: first prove directly that the positive-root subset of any commutative-group submonoid is a submonoid: products use the product of the two positive exponents. Thus the declared saturation closure is precisely that root subset. Bijective homomorphisms carry it to the corresponding root subset, and saturation of Q times a group is saturation(Q) times that group. Apply these facts to the proved ordinary chart equality. The restriction of the actual completion map gives an isomorphism of saturated charts with the sharp chart times the unit group. On Associates, projection and inclusion at unit coordinate 1 are inverse: their composite differs from the original element by the explicit unit with coordinate (1,u). This proves the sharp equivalence without importing the finite-saturation or localization-section theorem for this algebraic clause; those remain relevant to the global geometric assertions.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, 3.1.21, 3.1.24--3.1.25(ii), pp.101--102; saturation and the localized sharp structure sheaves.

proof.text: The comparison of Step 5 is canonical. In intrinsic terms it sends the class of a fraction $p-p_a$ to the class of $q(p)-a$; on saturation use the group homomorphism induced by $q$. If $j'$ is another splitting, then $\delta(b)=j'(b)-j(b)$ lies in $U$ and is additive, hence extends to $\delta:B^{\mathrm{gp}}\to U$. The two coordinate descriptions differ by $(c,u)\mapsto(c,u+\delta(c))$ (or its inverse). This change is the identity after sharpening. Replacing a lift $p_a$ by $p_a+v$, $v\in U$, changes each fraction by $-v$, again a unit. Choosing a different finite generating set does not change the monoids generated by all $b-a$, $b\in J$; all refinements have these same intrinsic fraction maps. Thus neither the splitting nor the representatives enter the sharp comparison. Lean proof by S6: compare the first projection of splitCompletion with the Grothendieck-group lift of Associates.mk by the universal extension equivalence and its equation on every numerator. This proves the intrinsic ambient-element formula in the statement. Any second sharp equivalence satisfying that formula has the same value on every Associates.mk x: its output representative and the constructed representative have equal ambient values, hence are equal by subtype extensionality. Quotient induction and homomorphism extensionality give equality of equivalences. In particular the formula contains neither the chosen splitting nor a choice of finite representatives.

source.place: VIII 3.1.25(ii), p.102, chart comparison; independence of choices written as explicit unit changes.

proof.text:
For $a,b\in J$, before saturation one has inside $B^{\mathrm{gp}}$
$$C_a[(b-a)^{-1}]=C_b[(a-b)^{-1}].$$
Indeed $c-a=(c-b)+(b-a)$ and $c-b=(c-a)+(a-b)$ for every $c\in J$, while the localized monoids contain both $b-a$ and $a-b$. Saturation commutes with these localizations by the finite-saturation lemma. In the product with $U$ the identical calculation applies, and the projections of Step 5 commute with it. Hence the sharp comparisons agree on each overlap specified in the blowup definitions. On a triple overlap every map sends a fraction to the same group-completion element, so the cocycle is the identity. The gluing definition now supplies inverse global maps by applying these mutually inverse local maps to agreeing tuples of sections. Restricting to a basic open merely localizes the same identities. This gives the claimed canonical isomorphism over $F$, compatible with arbitrary open restrictions, since basic opens cover them. Lean proof by S6 for all three displayed overlap equalities: prove the ordinary chart inclusion generator by generator using (z/b)*(b/a)=z/a. For saturation, normal-form induction in closure(Q union {d}) gives y*(d inverse)^k in Q. If x^(m+1) has that form and d inverse is already in Q, multiply the witness by ((d inverse)^k)^m to see (x*(d inverse)^k)^(m+1) in Q. Thus x belongs to closure(saturation(Q) union {d}). Apply this to d=b/a; its inverse a/b belongs to the b-chart because a is in the ideal. Closure inclusions now prove both pair equalities. For triple overlaps use the same saturated-chart inclusion and the identity (a/b)*(b/c)=a/c. Reverse the roles of a and b for the other inclusion. All equalities are in the original ambient completion, so the resulting transitions and cocycle are literal identity maps. This avoids using finite saturation for the displayed overlap formulas, while the global gluing and torsion-free claims remain open.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, 3.1.19, 3.1.25(ii), pp.101--102; overlap identity and gluing expanded.

proof.text: The saturated blowup remains in $\mathscr C$. Over a finite affine cover of $M$, take finitely many ideal generators on each chart. The corresponding finitely many saturated charts cover the blowup by its definition and are fine by the finite-saturation lemma. Each such chart is a submonoid of $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ containing $P$; hence its group completion, and that of each localization stalk, is the original torsion-free group $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$. At a prime of a saturated chart $R$, the complement $H$ is a face. The fs face-sharpening lemma states that $R-H$ is fine saturated and that its sharp quotient has finite free group completion. It gives exactly the torsion-free sharp stalk group required by $\mathscr C$. This also explains why new units in a blowup chart cause no failure of the hypothesis.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, Remark 3.1.20, 3.1.21, pp.101--102; sharp fs stalks as in VI 3.7(a), p.75.

proof.text: Induct on the length of the specified ordered fan tower. At length zero use $M$ with its given sharpening $F$. Suppose the corresponding monoscheme and canonical sharp comparison have been constructed through index $i$. Pull the specified next fan ideal back along that comparison and take its unique inverse image under the ideal bijection of Step 2. Blow up and saturate at this center. Steps 7 and 8 give the required next comparison and keep the next monoscheme in $\mathscr C$, so the induction continues. Any second construction has the same center after the comparison at index $i$, and the same glued saturated chart construction gives its canonical identification at index $i+1$. This proves uniqueness in the asserted sense. Starting instead with a monoscheme tower and sharpening recovers the same ideals and chart morphisms by Steps 2 and 7. No index has been removed, including stages with whole center.

source.place: VIII 3.1.22 and 3.1.25(iii), pp.101--102; length induction with centers retained.

proof.text:
To check maps, work on affine neighborhoods for a monoscheme morphism, with monoid homomorphism $h:P\to Q$. If $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ generate the source ideal, their images generate the pulled-back ideal. On the chart indexed by $p_a$, the map to the pulled-back chart sends
$$p\longmapsto h(p),\qquad p_i-p_a\longmapsto h(p_i)-h(p_a).$$
This homomorphism extends to saturation: for $nx$ in the source chart, $n h^{\mathrm{gp}}(x)$ is in the target chart, so $h^{\mathrm{gp}}(x)$ is in its saturation. It extends to overlaps by sending a denominator to the image of that denominator. Modulo units the formula is precisely the same one for the induced map of sharp monoids, by Steps 2 and 6. On chart refinements all these maps still have the displayed values, so they glue and commute with restriction. This proves the single-stage comparison for recursive pullback, in particular along the smooth morphisms in the statement; no assertion about arbitrary fiber products is used. Lean formalization of the fraction-substitution clause: let phi be the actual Grothendieck-group lift of h. The universal extension equation computes phi on all numerators. The closure universal property gives blowupChart(P,E,a) <= phi inverse image blowupChart(Q,E′,h(a)); the image-of-generators hypothesis supplies the fraction generators. Applying phi to a positive-power witness and then using the closure universal property again gives the corresponding inclusion for the declared root-saturation closures. Restrict phi to these submonoids. Subtype extensionality proves uniqueness. This argument works for arbitrary commutative monoids, so the existing fineness hypotheses are retained but unused.

source.place: VIII 3.1.22--3.1.25, pp.101--102; substitutions giving the recursive pullback level maps.

proof.text: Apply Step 10 at each inherited index in the induction of Step 9. At index zero the comparison is the given sharpening map; if the comparison square commutes at index $i$, Step 2 identifies the pulled-back next centers and Step 10 identifies the next saturated charts and their maps. Thus it commutes at index $i+1$. For identity maps every fraction is unchanged; for a composite $k\circ h$, the two substitutions both send $p_i-p_a$ to $k(h(p_i))-k(h(p_a))$, and agree also on saturated elements by their group homomorphisms. The recursive comparisons therefore respect identities and composition, while keeping the ordered centers and every original index. The length-zero case and the empty underlying monoscheme satisfy the same formulas with no charts to check. This proves all tower and pullback assertions. Lean formalization of the recursive-pullback clause: use the level torsion-free conclusions of sharpening_saturated_tower_comparison for both given towers. Define the new lift at i to be exactly (p.lift i).toFan. Each original blowup center is nonempty coherent and hence coherent after forgetting positivity of its finite generating list. The ideal-pullback equality in sharpening_blowup_ideal_comparison, together with p.centers, supplies each new center equation. Apply sharpSpaceMap to p.commutes and use the published composition law for sharpSpaceMap to supply the commuting squares. Two PullbackTower structures with the same lifts are equal, since the other fields are proofs. The identity and composition conclusions are precisely the published sharpSpaceMap laws. This uses only the existing canonical-map API, not SharpeningGeometry or the rule bijection; it does not require the smoothness assumption, which stays in the original signature.

source.place: VIII 3.1.22, 3.1.25(iii), pp.101--102; recursive compatibility and identities/composition.

proof_origin.place: Expose VIII 3.1.17--3.1.25, pp.101--102; the proof of 3.1.25 expanded in fraction charts, with the existing fine-monoid unit-splitting, finite-saturation, face-sharpening and affine-section lemmas. Partial Lean proof by G9: fraction substitution is constructed directly by two closure inclusions; recursive tower pullback is assembled from the existing ideal/tower comparison clauses and canonical sharpening-map laws. The other six named theorem holes keep the stated source plan. S6 completed the entire algebraic product-chart comparison and ordinary/saturated/triple-overlap comparison directly from the declared fraction-chart and root-saturation constructions. Both proofs and their private helpers are sorry-free; no additional proof imports, axioms, definitions, public declarations, or split nodes are added. Four geometric theorem holes remain unchanged.
